info.title: Claude Headless API
info.summary: OpenAI-compatible LLM API backed by Claude Code's headless mode (`claude -p`).
info.description:
Claude Headless API exposes Claude through an **OpenAI-compatible** HTTP interface. Every completion
is produced by running Claude Code in headless mode (`claude -p`) inside the server's container, so
any OpenAI SDK works by pointing its `base_url` at this server.

**Highlights**

- Choose the model (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable` or a full model id) and the effort
  (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`) on every request.
- **Sessions** keep a conversation on the server: each turn resumes the same Claude Code session, so you
  only send the new message.
- Claude runs with **no tools**: it behaves like a plain text model and cannot run commands or read files.

**Authentication.** Every `/v1` endpoint needs an API token created by an administrator in the dashboard
(`/admin`). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (preferred) or `x-api-key: <token>`. Tokens look
like `chk_…`, may expire, may be limited to some models or to a maximum effort, and have a per-minute
rate limit.

**Errors** use OpenAI's shape — `{"error": {"message", "type", "param", "code"}}` — see the `Error` schema
for every `type` and `code` this server returns.

**Streaming:** send `stream: true` to receive the reply as OpenAI-style server-sent events
(`chat.completion.chunk`, then `data: [DONE]`), as OpenAI SDKs expect.

**Not supported:** image or audio input, tool/function calling, `n > 1`,
and sampling controls (`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `stop`, …), which are accepted and ignored.
See `docs/missing-features.md` in the repository for the full list.

servers.description: Local deployment (`docker compose up -d`). Replace with your server's address.

tags.name: Sessions
tags.description:
Conversations kept on the server. The first turn starts a Claude Code session
(`claude -p --session-id <uuid>`); every later turn resumes it (`claude -p --resume <uuid>`), so Claude
keeps the real conversation and its prompt cache. Sessions belong to the **user** who owns the token:
any of that user's tokens can use them, and nobody else's can. Turns within one session run one at a time.

tags.description: Models this server lets your token use.

tags.name: Meta
tags.description: Health check and this specification. No authentication required.

post.description:
Sends the conversation in `messages` to Claude and returns one assistant reply.

- `system` and `developer` messages are joined into Claude's system prompt. Without one, the server's
  default system prompt (Settings in the dashboard) is used.
- Earlier `user`/`assistant` turns are passed to Claude as a transcript ahead of the final user message,
  which must be the last non-system message.
- `effort` takes precedence over `reasoning_effort`. Without either, the server default is used.
- Set `session_id` to keep the conversation on the server instead of re-sending history: `"new"` starts a
  session and the response carries its id; an existing id continues it. With `session_id`, only the
  **last** user message is sent and `response_format` is ignored.

**Streaming.** With `stream: true` the reply arrives as server-sent events (`text/event-stream`), each a
`data:` line holding a `chat.completion.chunk`: first `delta: {role: "assistant"}`, then pieces of
`delta.content` as Claude writes them, then `finish_reason: "stop"`, and finally `data: [DONE]`. With
`stream_options: {include_usage: true}`, a last chunk with `usage` and empty `choices` comes before
`[DONE]`.

- Failures before any text (bad key, unknown model, Claude not logged in, …) still return the normal
  JSON error with its status code.
- A failure after text was sent arrives as one `data: {"error": {…}}` event, with no `[DONE]`.
- If the client disconnects, the run is stopped; a session turn interrupted that way is not stored.

**Web search.** Send `web_search_options` (`{}` is enough) to let Claude use Claude Code's WebSearch tool
for this request. It works only if an admin turned on "Allow web search" in Settings; otherwise the
request fails with `400 web_search_disabled`. The search runs on Anthropic's side, and Claude decides
whether and what to search, so `search_context_size` and `user_location` are accepted and ignored.
Searching adds cost and latency. Without `web_search_options`, Claude runs with no tools.

- Non-streamed, `content` is the final answer only. Streamed, any text Claude wrote before it
  searched ("Let me look that up.") also arrives, separated from the answer by a blank line.
- Claude can't fetch pages (no WebFetch): it answers from the search results.

Unknown OpenAI parameters (`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `stop`, `seed`, …) are accepted and
ignored, because `claude -p` has no equivalent. Each call counts towards the token's rate limit and is
recorded in the request log.

messages.content: What is the capital of Morocco?
You are a concise assistant. Answer in one sentence.
Extract the city and country from "I live in Rabat, Morocco."
Let's study fractions. Start with the basics.

streamed.summary: Streamed reply, with usage at the end

messages.content: What changed in the latest Python release? Cite your sources.

message.content: The capital of Morocco is Rabat.
A fraction describes part of a whole…

schema.description:
Sent when `stream` is true. Each event is a `data:` line with a `ChatCompletionChunk` (see
Schemas), ending with `data: [DONE]`; or a `data:` line with an `Error` if the run fails part way.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
Python (openai)
x-codeSamples.source:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="chk_...")

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="sonnet",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "Answer in one sentence."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of Morocco?"},
    ],
    reasoning_effort="low",  # or extra_body={"effort": "xhigh"} for every Claude level
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)

# Keep the conversation on the server instead of re-sending history:
first = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="sonnet",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Remember the number 42."}],
    extra_body={"session_id": "new"},
)
session_id = first.model_extra["session_id"]
again = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="sonnet",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Which number did I ask you to remember?"}],
    extra_body={"session_id": session_id},
)
print(again.choices[0].message.content)

# Let Claude search the web (an admin must allow it in Settings):
news = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="sonnet",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What changed in the latest Python release?"}],
    web_search_options={},
)
print(news.choices[0].message.content)

x-codeSamples.label: JavaScript (fetch)
cURL (streaming)
x-codeSamples.source:
# -N turns off curl's buffering so chunks print as they arrive
curl -N http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "sonnet", "stream": true, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a haiku about Rabat."}]}'

post.summary: Send a message in a session
post.description:
Sends one user message and returns Claude's reply in the `chat.completion` shape, plus `session_id`.
Only this message is sent to Claude: the history lives in Claude Code's own transcript, which is
resumed. `model` and `effort` may change from turn to turn and become the session's new defaults.

Both the message and the reply are stored and can be read back with `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}`.
A failed turn stores nothing, so it can simply be retried. Counts towards the rate limit.

Send `stream: true` for server-sent events, exactly as on `POST /v1/chat/completions` (every chunk also
carries `session_id`). A streamed turn that fails or is cut off by a disconnect is not stored, and the
session's next turn rebuilds the conversation from the stored messages.

Send `web_search_options` to let Claude search the web for this turn, as on chat completions. A turn
without it, after one that searched, rebuilds the conversation from the stored messages instead of
resuming Claude's transcript, so it misses the prompt cache once.

example.content: Now explain how to add 1/3 and 1/4.

message.content: Find a common denominator: 1/3 = 4/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, so the sum is 7/12.

schema.description:
Sent when `stream` is true. Each event is a `data:` line with a `ChatCompletionChunk` (see
Schemas), ending with `data: [DONE]`; or a `data:` line with an `Error` if the run fails part way.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/sessions/$SESSION_ID/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"content": "Now explain how to add 1/3 and 1/4."}'

x-codeSamples.label: Python (requests)
x-codeSamples.source:
import requests

BASE = "http://localhost:8000/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer chk_..."}

session_id = requests.post(f"{BASE}/sessions", json={"model": "sonnet"}, headers=HEADERS).json()["id"]

def say(text: str) -> str:
    r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/sessions/{session_id}/messages", json={"content": text}, headers=HEADERS)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

print(say("Remember the number 42."))
print(say("Which number did I ask you to remember?"))

get.description:
A compact Markdown brief for LLM agents that call this API: authentication, choosing a model and effort,
stateless calls vs sessions, and a retry policy for every error code. It follows the `llms.txt`
convention and is the same text as `docs/agent-api-guide.md`, with this server's address filled in.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source: curl http://localhost:8000/llms.txt

bearerAuth.description:
API token created in the admin dashboard, sent as `Authorization: Bearer chk_…`. The token is shown
once when it is created; the server stores only its hash.

apiKeyHeader.name: x-api-key
apiKeyHeader.description: The same API token, for clients that cannot set an `Authorization` header.

SessionId.name: session_id
SessionId.description: The session id returned when the session was created.

Effort.description:
How much effort Claude spends, passed to `claude --effort`. Higher effort thinks longer and costs
more. A token may be capped at a maximum effort.

ReasoningEffort.description:
OpenAI's `reasoning_effort`, accepted for SDK compatibility. `none` and `minimal` map to `low`; the
other values map to the Claude effort of the same name. Ignored when `effort` is set.

ContentPart.description: One part of a multi-part message. Only `text` parts are supported; any other type is rejected with `400`.

MessageContent.description: Message text, either as a string or as an array of text parts (joined with newlines).

role.description:
`system` and `developer` messages form the system prompt; `user` and `assistant` messages form the
conversation. `tool` and `function` messages are rejected because tools are disabled.

json_schema.description: OpenAI's wrapper: `{name, schema, strict}`. Only `schema` is used.

schema.description: A JSON Schema the reply must satisfy.

model.description:
Model alias (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`) or full model id. Must be enabled on the server and
allowed for the token. Defaults to the server's default model.

messages.description: The conversation so far. The last non-system message must have role `user`.

stream.description: Send the reply as server-sent events (`chat.completion.chunk`s, then `data: [DONE]`).

session_id.description:
Extension. `"new"` starts a server-side session; an existing session id continues it. With a session,
only the last user message is sent and the response includes `session_id`. See the Sessions endpoints.

additionalProperties.description: Other OpenAI parameters (`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `stop`, `seed`, …) are accepted and ignored.

WebSearchOptions.description:
Present (even as `{}`): Claude may search the web for this request with Claude Code's WebSearch tool.
The server must allow it ("Allow web search" in Settings), or the request fails with
`400 web_search_disabled`. The fields are OpenAI's; they are accepted and ignored, because Claude decides
what to search.

StreamOptions.description: Options for a streamed reply (`stream` true).

include_usage.description: Add a final chunk with `usage` and empty `choices` before `data: [DONE]`.

ChatCompletionChunk.description: One server-sent event of a streamed reply. All chunks of a reply share `id` and `created`.

choices.description: One choice, or none on the final usage chunk.

delta.description: `role` on the first chunk, then `content` pieces; empty on the last chunk.

finish_reason.description: `null` until the last chunk, which has `stop`.

session_id.description: Present on every chunk when the reply belongs to a session.

created.description: Unix time (seconds) the reply was produced.

content.description: The reply text (a JSON string when `response_format` is `json_schema`).

session_id.description: Present only when the reply belongs to a session.

Usage.description:
Token counts reported by Claude Code. `prompt_tokens` includes cached input, and Claude Code's own
system prompt and context count towards it, so it is larger than the text you sent.

prompt_tokens.description: Input tokens, including cache reads and cache writes.

cached_tokens.description: Input tokens served from Claude's prompt cache.

created.description: Always `0`; aliases have no fixed release date.

SessionCreate.description: All fields are optional; send `{}` for a session with server defaults.

model.description: Default model for the session's turns. Defaults to the server's default model.

system_prompt.description: System prompt for the whole conversation. Cannot be changed later. Defaults to the server's default system prompt.

title.description: Display title. Defaults to the start of the first message.

model.description: Model for this turn. Defaults to the session's current model.

stream.description: Send the reply as server-sent events, as on chat completions.

id.description: Session id, used in the session URLs.

title.description: Display title; `null` until set or until the first message.

model.description: Model used by the latest turn, and the default for the next one.

system_prompt.description: The session's system prompt; `null` means the server default.

created_at.description: Unix time (seconds) the session was created.

updated_at.description: Unix time (seconds) of the latest turn.

message_count.description: Number of stored messages (two per turn).

input_tokens.description: Uncached input tokens summed over all turns.

output_tokens.description: Output tokens summed over all turns.

total_cost_usd.description: Cost reported by Claude Code, summed over all turns.

code.description:
Machine-readable reason:

- `missing_api_key`, `invalid_api_key`, `api_key_revoked`, `api_key_expired` — 401
- `user_disabled`, `model_not_allowed`, `effort_not_allowed` — 403
- `model_not_found`, `web_search_disabled` — 400 (other 400s have `null`)
- `session_not_found` — 404
- `rate_limit_exceeded` — 429
- `upstream_error` — 500/502, `timeout` — 504 (also sent inside a stream that fails part way)

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed or asks for something this server does not support.

error.message: Model 'gpt-4' is not available. Available: opus, sonnet, haiku.

webSearchDisabled.summary: Web search not allowed on this server

error.message: Web search is not enabled on this server.
Content part type 'image_url' is not supported; only text is.

Unauthorized.description: The API token is missing, unknown, revoked or expired.

Forbidden.description: The token's user is disabled, or the token may not use this model or effort.

error.message: This API key may not use model 'opus'.

SessionNotFound.description: No session with this id belongs to the token's user.

RateLimited.description: The token sent more requests in the last minute than its limit allows.

error.message: Rate limit of 60 requests/minute exceeded. Retry in 12s.

ServerError.description: The server could not start the Claude CLI (misconfigured installation).

UpstreamError.description: Claude Code ran but failed — for example it is not logged in, the model is unknown, or the budget cap was hit.

error.message: Claude CLI error: Not logged in · Please run /login

Timeout.description: Claude did not answer within the server's request timeout; the run was stopped.
